# Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Implementation Specification > Implementation companion to `OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md`. > > Scope: define the smallest complete first build of Ocean Desktop's Dynamic > Island and its keyboard-first session focus/search mode. This is deliberately > concrete: data contracts, components, files, state transitions, keyboard > routing, CSS geometry, acceptance checks, and explicitly deferred work. > > The practical delivery sequence and commit gates live in > [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md). ## Decision summary Build this before a permanent left rail. The first release is **not** a generalized desktop task system. It is a Tauri-only, titlebar-adjacent focus surface backed by the existing daemon session catalogue. ### V1 ships - compact Dynamic Island in the desktop header - focused session identity plus a count of active-background sessions - click to open an Island overlay - overlay lists active/recent sessions with project/path/branch/origin metadata - selecting a result calls the existing `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and moves that session into the center transcript - `⌘P` opens that same overlay in search mode - fuzzy search over existing session metadata - arrow keys, Enter, Escape, click-outside behavior ### V1 does not ship - inline reply to a background session - cross-session live streaming in the Island - server-side/session-content semantic search - approvals, CI, GitHub, browser, rooms, Council, files, or PR results - a left rail - a replacement for the existing web/extension Sessions modal Those are follow-on waves after the core focus interaction is proven. ## Phase 2A — approved read-only attention slice V1 proved the focus loop. The next slice turns the expanded Island into a truthful cross-session activity surface without giving it mutation authority. This section is binding for Phase 2A. ### Authoritative sources Use the daemon's existing global snapshots: - `GET /v1/requests` for queued, running, waiting-for-permission, cancelling, and errored request state across sessions. - `GET /v1/permissions` for currently pending permissions and their request/session/tool/reason metadata. - `GET /v1/agent/sessions` remains the title/project/path lookup catalogue. Poll the two attention snapshots every three seconds while the Tauri Island is mounted, refresh immediately on mount and overlay open, and retain the last good snapshot if one request fails. This is an interim read-only projection, not a new runtime store. A unified replayable daemon attention stream remains the later target. Never infer running, blocked, failed, or complete state from session timestamps. Timestamps may order authoritative items; they may not create them. ### Projection rules Project the snapshot into these display states: - `NeedsHuman`: every pending permission; de-duplicate its matching `waiting_for_permission` request. - `Running`: queued or running requests. - `Cancelling`: cancelling requests. - `Failed`: the three newest errored requests in the current daemon registry. - Omit completed and cancelled requests. Join `session_id` to the fetched session catalogue for title/project display. Use a short session id fallback when the catalogue has not caught up. Do not render raw permission `args` in the Island; the existing transcript-adjacent permission surface remains the detail/action authority. ### Compact-state priority The closed chip preserves the focused session title. Its trailing status reads, in priority order: 1. ` need attention` for `NeedsHuman` items only 2. ` running` for `Running` items only 3. existing ` recent` Failed and cancelling items remain visible in expanded Activity but do not make the compact chip claim that they need human input or are still running. The dot uses `--warn` for human attention, the existing live accent for running, and a neutral/empty treatment otherwise. No pulse or decorative animation. The accessible label and one polite live region announce the same factual count. ### Expanded interaction The popover remains one dialog and one material surface. When activity exists, render an `Activity` section between search and session results: - needs-human items first, then failed, cancelling, and running; - one plain summary row per item, with state, session title, and concise detail; - clicking or pressing Enter on a summary toggles its inline disclosure; - the disclosure may show project, tool/request state, and bounded reason; - one ghost `Open session` action focuses the associated session through `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and closes the Island. Attention controls participate in a real Tab focus trap. Arrow-key/ `aria-activedescendant` session navigation remains scoped to the search input, so using a disclosure button can never accidentally switch the selected session. Escape still closes exactly one surface and restores the invoking focus. ### Explicit Phase 2A deferrals - no approve/deny inside the Island; - no inline reply/resume or stop action; - no local dismiss/read state; - no raw permission arguments; - no browser, CI, GitHub, room, or Council cards; - no claim that the polling projection is durable attention history. Those mutations follow only after the read-only state and ordering prove useful and their daemon authorization contracts are explicit. ## Phase 3A — submitter-authorized permission actions The first mutation slice adds Approve/Deny only when this exact Surface owns the turn's decision token. The public permission snapshot never exposes that token, and the Island must not weaken the daemon's authorization boundary. An expanded permission card is actionable only when all are true: - its `permission_id` exists in the focused Surface's live `pending_permissions` signal; - the permission belongs to the currently focused session; - `active_decision_token` is present for that submitted turn. When actionable, the disclosure shows one compact action row: danger-ghost `Deny` followed by primary `Approve`. Both reuse `Daemon::decide_permission`, disable while deciding, and never add raw arguments to the Island. The redundant `Open session` action is hidden because the owning session is already focused. A background or foreign-surface permission stays read-only and offers only `Open session`; it must never render a button that will predictably fail token verification. `Allow for session`, inline reply, background stop, and dismiss/acknowledge remain deferred. This slice changes no daemon endpoint or token semantics. ## Future typed cards — CI, diffs, and todos CI/GitHub and todo disclosures follow the same plain-row grammar, but require new daemon-owned typed payloads rather than parsing logs or inventing local state. A CI summary may show repository, branch, check state, duration, and bounded pass/fail counts. Its disclosure may lazily load changed-file `+/-` summaries, a small bounded diff excerpt, and one `Open full run/diff` action. Never render a whole patch or raw build log inside the Island. Rerun/cancel actions require explicit daemon capabilities and permission policy. A todo summary may show `completed / total`; its disclosure is a compact checklist. It remains read-only until the daemon publishes durable todo ids and a mutation contract. The Island never derives durable todos from transcript text or transient tool output. ## Existing foundations to reuse Do not recreate these systems: | Existing implementation | Reuse in Island work | | --- | --- | | `Daemon::sessions: RwSignal>` | search corpus and list data | | `Daemon::session_id: RwSignal>` | focused-session identity | | `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` | sole session focus/switch operation | | `sessions.rs::split_origin`, `fmt_relative_time`, `session_root`, project lookup | display metadata and normalized search text | | `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` behavior | fuzzy scoring semantics; extract/move to a shared search helper rather than copy it | | `PaletteView` keyboard pattern | input autofocus, ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, backdrop click | | `app.rs` `window_event_listener(ev::keydown, ...)` | `⌘P` global shortcut and overlay Escape priority | | `host::running_in_tauri()` | mount/gating boundary | | `styles/chrome.css` titlebar model | titlebar position and drag-region rules | Important fact: today `Daemon::switch_session` replaces the active transcript and reconnects its SSE/permission streams. The Island must call it; it must not attempt a second transcript/session runtime of its own. ## User-facing model ### Terminology - **Focused session**: the daemon's current `session_id`; it owns the center transcript and composer. - **Background session**: any other persisted session in the catalogue. V1 treats "recent" as the only reliable activity signal. - **Island**: compact titlebar control plus its expanded overlay. - **Search mode**: overlay opened by `⌘P`, with input focused. - **Browse mode**: overlay opened by click, with input present but not focused or visually secondary. Do not call every session "active" in V1. The client currently observes an SSE stream only for the focused session, so it cannot truthfully determine whether other sessions are presently generating work. Use **recent sessions** until the daemon publishes cross-session activity. ### V1 interaction flow ```text Focused center session: A Catalogue: A, B, C, D header Island (closed) [ A · Ocean Surface · 3 recent ] click Island OR press ⌘P → Island overlay opens → list shows A, B, C, D ordered by focus/recentness choose B + Enter/click → Daemon::switch_session(B.id, B.title) → B becomes focused center session → overlay closes → A remains in the catalogue and appears in future Island results ``` No extra "slotting" persistence is needed for V1. The natural catalogue order already makes the old focused session available. Explicit pins/orbits can arrive later only if observed usage requires them. ## Data model Create a new `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` module. ### Core types ```rust #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum IslandMode { Closed, Browse, Search, } #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub enum IslandPriority { Focused, Recent, Background, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct IslandSession { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub project: Option, pub cwd: String, pub branch: Option, pub origin: Option, pub updated_at: String, pub turn_count: u32, pub is_focused: bool, pub priority: IslandPriority, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub enum IslandResult { Session(IslandSession), } ``` Keep V1's result enum even though it has one variant. It establishes the extension seam for `Approval`, `BrowserTask`, `CiRun`, `File`, and `GitHubPull` without forcing speculative implementations today. ### Derivation function Expose a pure function in `island.rs`: ```rust pub(crate) fn derive_island_sessions( sessions: &[SessionSummary], projects: &[ProjectInfo], focused_id: Option<&str>, ) -> Vec; ``` Rules: 1. Retain every daemon-catalogued session, including zero-turn drafts. This follows `sessions.rs::group_for_panel` parity. 2. Resolve project display name via `owning_project`, then `project_for_root`. 3. Parse `[WEB]`, `[?]`, etc. title prefix using a reusable public helper from `sessions.rs` or a new shared metadata module. Do not duplicate parsing. Blank daemon titles use the Sessions panel's `(untitled)` fallback so a zero-turn draft never renders as an apparently broken empty Island. 4. Sort: - focused session first, - then `updated_at` newest-first, - stable tie-breaker by title/id. 5. `priority` is `Focused` for focused session; `Recent` for sessions updated in the existing `is_recent` window; `Background` otherwise. 6. No claims about remote/live activity in V1. ### Search document and scoring Create a testable pure helper: ```rust pub(crate) fn island_search_text(item: &IslandSession) -> String; pub(crate) fn search_island( query: &str, items: &[IslandSession], ) -> Vec; ``` Search text joins, lowercased, with separators: ```text title project cwd branch origin state turns ``` Examples that must work: ```text north star project:ocean-surface // V1 literal text match is enough; facets deferred src/app.rs main tauri recent ``` Scoring: - empty query: existing derivation order - exact/prefix match in title: strongest boost - project match: second boost - cwd/branch/origin: normal fuzzy score - focused item: tie-break boost, not enough to hide better matches - recency: tie-break boost Extract `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` and the word-boundary helper into either: - `src/search.rs` (recommended), or - `pub(crate)` helpers in `palette.rs` Use the same scorer rather than making `⌘P` feel inconsistent with `⌘K`. ## Component API and ownership ### `Island` component ```rust #[component] pub fn Island( daemon: Daemon, mode: RwSignal, ) -> impl IntoView ``` `app.rs` owns `mode`, because it coordinates: - header click - `⌘P` - global Escape ordering - any future deep links / menu actions `Island` owns local overlay state: ```rust let query = RwSignal::new(String::new()); let selected_index = RwSignal::new(0usize); let input_ref = NodeRef::::new(); ``` ### Required component DOM shape ```text section.island-host // mounted inside .ocean-header button.island-chip // compact/default state focused session identity background/recent count state dot Show(mode != Closed) div.island-scrim // full window click target, below header section.island-popover // anchored below chip form / div island-search input.island-search__input div.island-results div.island-group button.island-result ``` Important: render `island-host` inside the header so the chip naturally occupies the titlebar zone. Add a new command registry entry: ```rust Command { id: "focus-search", title: "Search Ocean…".into(), hint: Some("⌘P".into()), scope: CommandScope::App, slash: None, enabled: Signal::derive(move || in_tauri), run: Callback::new(move |_| island_mode.set(IslandMode::Search)), } ``` This makes the action discoverable in `⌘K` and native menubar work later while preserving the semantic separation: `⌘K` invokes the search surface; `⌘P` is the direct shortcut. ### No transcript/composer changes in V1 Do not remove the Sessions landing action or alter the composer in the Island first slice. Respect IME composition if the app already exposes an equivalent guard; otherwise add it before intercepting the shortcut. ## CSS implementation Create `styles/island.css`; add it to `index.html` after `chrome.css` and before `panels.css`. Also add it to any explicit extension-style copy/build list only if the build requires every stylesheet to exist there. The component does not mount off-Tauri, so it remains visually inert on web/extension. ### Geometry tokens ```css :root { --island-max-w: 360px; --island-popover-w: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px)); --island-top: 64px; /* header bottom + seam; revise against live Tauri shot */ } ``` ### Required layering ```text workspace pane 50 web deck 60 modal sessions 100 Island scrim/popover 120 command palette 1100 ``` The Island must sit above the workspace and ordinary panels, below `⌘K` palette. This means opening `⌘K` visually wins even if Island search is open; opening the palette should close Island as a small follow-up hardening task. ### Styling constraints - Island chip uses the existing OCEAN depth ramp, not iOS visual imitation. - No giant pill and no floating dashboard card. - Use a compact rounded capsule only because it communicates one living, titlebar-adjacent object. - Popover is a single elevated material surface with a crisp border; result rows use tone changes, not individually elevated cards. - Header must remain draggable around the Island. Keep left/right noninteractive zones as `data-tauri-drag-region`; explicitly omit it on chip, input, and rows. - At `< 840px` desktop width, reduce chip metadata to title + count. At widths too narrow for a usable popover, allow the fixed overlay to span the safe viewport width; do not introduce a different mobile design in this slice. ### Initial selectors ```css .ocean-header { position: relative; } .island-host { position: absolute; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-chip { /* compact titlebar control */ } .island-scrim { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 120; } .island-popover { position: fixed; do not move panel UI | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/palette.rs` | move fuzzy scorer to a shared module or expose it safely; no duplicated score algorithm | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | recommended new shared fuzzy scorer if extraction is clean | | `styles/island.css` | new Island geometry and skin | | `index.html` | add stylesheet link | | extension build/style wiring | only if stylesheet packaging explicitly requires it | | `docs/OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md` | already records product direction; Start Tauri app with ≥4 persisted sessions across ≥2 projects. 2. Verify chip is centered and does not overlap traffic lights, runtime controls, or workspace toggle. 3. Click chip: browse overlay opens, shows focused session first. 4. Click outside: closes. 5. Press `⌘P` from composer, workspace, and header: search opens and input has focus each time. 6. Type project, branch, title, cwd, and origin queries; confirm expected result. 7. Arrow down/up/Enter switches session and overlay closes. 8. Confirm old session is available when opening Island again. 9. Confirm `⌘K` palette still works and Escape closes exactly the topmost open surface. 10. Resize Tauri to narrow and wide widths; verify usable overlay geometry. 11. Verify browser PWA and extension preserve their existing Sessions-modal and browser-print behavior. ## Build sequence / commits Do not put all behavior in one giant commit. ### Commit 1 — Pure Island index - new `island.rs` types/derivation/search helpers - extract shared fuzzy score - unit tests only - no UI **Exit:** `cargo test` for the UI crate passes. ### Commit 2 — Island visual shell - component mounts on Tauri header - closed/browse state - display derived session rows - click row switches session - CSS and stylesheet wiring **Exit:** click-only interaction works; web has no visual change. ### Commit 3 — `⌘P` search mode - global shortcut - search input/focus - filtering, selection, keyboard navigation - Escape priority - registry discoverability command **Exit:** keyboard-only session focus switching works. ### Commit 4 — Live desktop polish - inspect an actual Tauri screenshot - tune titlebar spacing, type scale, row density, result limit, focus ring - run narrow/wide regressions **Exit:** the control feels built into the native shell rather than pasted over web chrome. ## Follow-up contract: required daemon work before richer Island states Do not fake background activity with only timestamps. The Island is a reducer/view of that stream. This preserves the existing many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture and prevents a Tauri-only notion of work state. ## Explicit non-goal guardrails - Do not build inline quick reply until the daemon supports a safe background session prompt lifecycle or explicit foreground handoff semantics. - Do not add a local-only session index that diverges from daemon state. - Do not overload `⌘P` with generic mutating commands; that is `⌘K`. - Do not remove Sessions modal or add a rail until Island use is observed. - Do not impersonate macOS/iOS Dynamic Island visuals.
